channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: European Union Opposes Trump's Plans for Security Deal with Russia
item.description: The EU, Poland, and Ukraine have stated that the US and Russia cannot decide on European security without European involvement. This reaction follows US President Donald Trump's remarks about a potential agreement with Moscow that could affect all of Europe, not just Ukraine. Trump suggested a significant deal was imminent, though details were not disclosed.

item.title: Putin Announces Start Date for Russia-US-Ukraine Talks in UAE
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced that trilateral negotiations between Russia, the US, and Ukraine will commence on November 10 in the United Arab Emirates. The meetings, scheduled for November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi, are expected to focus on post-war security, de-escalation, humanitarian initiatives, and steps toward peace.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan Explore New Opportunities for Strategic Alignment
item.description: Tashkent hosted expert meetings discussing Kazakhstan's President Tokayev's address. Discussions focused on political and socio-economic priorities and deepening Uzbek-Kazakh cooperation. Experts from the International Institute of Central Asia and the University of World Economy and Diplomacy participated, alongside representatives from the Institute for Strategic and Regional Studies.

item.title: Teenager Sentenced to 15 Years for Knife Attack on Schoolgirl in Atyrau
item.description: A 16-year-old teenager in Atyrau has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for attempting to murder a 13-year-old schoolgirl. The court found he planned the attack, leaving notes about seeking revenge. He was found guilty of attempted murder of a minor.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Armenia Discuss TRIPP Corridor Transit Potential
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Transport, Assel Zhanasova, met with Armenian officials to discuss the transit potential of the TRIPP corridor. They explored developing TRIPP as an extension of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (Middle Corridor) and its integration with global logistics networks.

item.title: Almaty Teenager Dies a Week After Allergic Reaction to Antibiotic Test
item.description: A 14-year-old boy in Almaty has died a week after his condition rapidly deteriorated following an antibiotic sensitivity test at a clinic. The teenager's parents stated he had been ill with swollen lymph nodes and had undergone two courses of treatment without improvement. The police have opened a criminal case into the incident.

item.title: Tashkent Police Launch Investigation into Blogger Inciting Violence Against Singer
item.description: Tashkent's Internal Affairs Directorate has launched an investigation into a blogger whose video content is perceived as inciting violence, potentially calling for the murder of singer Mubinolo. The Nemolchi.Uz project had previously urged law enforcement to assess the video's content and the blogger's actions. The video depicts a scene of potential physical punishment and murder.

item.title: Aktobe Police Suspect Ex-Husband in Murder of 26-Year-Old Woman
item.description: In Aktobe, a 26-year-old woman was found strangled in her apartment. Her 31-year-old ex-husband has been detained on suspicion of murder. Relatives claim the man had a history of violence against the victim, which led to their divorce. Police are investigating the incident as a domestic conflict.

item.title: Uzbekistan Enhances Subsoil Use Transparency and Efficiency with Digital Technologies
item.description: Uzbekistan is prioritizing the improvement of mechanisms for searching, studying, and rationally developing mineral resources. The Ministry of Mining Industry and Geology is implementing digital technologies to increase the transparency and efficiency of subsoil use, simplifying procedures and expanding opportunities for entrepreneurs.

item.title: SCO Dialogue Plus on Security in Digital Transformation Concludes in Samarkand
item.description: The first SCO Dialogue Plus expert meeting on 'Security in the Era of Digital Transformation: Countering Terrorism and Extremism Amidst New Technologies' has concluded in Samarkand. The event, initiated by Uzbekistan's President Mirziyoyev, gathered security officials from 24 countries and international organizations to address emerging threats.

item.title: Uzbek President Concludes Working Visit to Astana, Attends AI Security Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has concluded his working visit to Astana, Kazakhstan. During the visit, he participated in a Central Asian leaders' meeting on artificial intelligence security within the Aqaba Process. He also held bilateral meetings with leaders from Jordan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Azerbaijan, and Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Tajikistan Seeks Iranian Oil Amid Russian Supply Concerns
item.description: Tajikistan has begun importing oil from Iran due to concerns about continuing Russian supplies. Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries have led Moscow to impose export restrictions, impacting Central Asian nations. Despite Russia being the primary energy supplier, Tajikistan is diversifying to mitigate risks and sustain its economy, even if it means risking U.S. sanctions on Iran.

item.title: Central Asian Leaders Discuss AI's Role in Enabling Terrorism
item.description: Leaders from Central Asia met in Astana to discuss how artificial intelligence can be used by militant groups for terrorism. Topics included AI's use in spreading propaganda, disinformation, aiding recruitment, and hindering investigations. Uzbekistan proposed hosting a UN counter-terrorism office to enhance regional cooperation on detecting terrorist content and financing.

item.title: Turkmen President Meets Jordanian King to Discuss Cooperation
item.description: Turkmen President Serdar Berdimuhamedow met with King Abdullah II of Jordan during a working visit to Kazakhstan. They expressed satisfaction with the opportunity to meet within the framework of the Central Asia Heads of State meeting on AI security. Both leaders emphasized their commitment to developing bilateral relations and strengthening mutually beneficial cooperation.

item.title: CIS Cultural Cooperation Council Holds Meeting in Ashgabat
item.description: The CIS Cultural Cooperation Council held its regular meeting in Ashgabat to assess the current state of cultural and humanitarian relations among member states and define future joint plans. The meeting aimed to strengthen historical and cultural ties, elevate spiritual and creative connections, and expand mutually beneficial cooperation within the CIS space.

item.title: International Theater Festival Opens in Ashgabat, Turkmenistan
item.description: The V International Theater Festival, themed 'Theater Art of the Era of Happiness,' has opened in Ashgabat. The festival brings together theater artists and creative groups from Kazakhstan, Russia, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Armenia, and other countries. This event highlights Turkmenistan's commitment to cultural exchange and promoting its national culture globally.

item.title: TBC Uzbekistan Reports Q3 2026 Financial Results Amid Ecosystem Growth
item.description: TBC Uzbekistan, a digital financial ecosystem part of TBC Bank Group, released its Q3 2026 IFRS results. The ecosystem, including TBC Bank and payment service Payme, saw growth in business clients and services. Registered users reached 25.5 million, with 6.1 million monthly active users. Payment volumes surged 46.5% year-on-year.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Meets with King of Jordan on Sidelines of Aqaba Process Meeting
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with King Abdullah II of Jordan in Astana during the Aqaba Process meeting. They discussed expanding bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade, investment, and cultural-humanitarian spheres. Both leaders acknowledged the platform's growing importance amid global threats.

item.title: Student Sentenced to 15 Years for Stabbing 13-Year-Old Girl in Atyrau School
item.description: A ninth-grade student in Atyrau has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for stabbing a 13-year-old girl in a school corridor. The incident occurred in March at the BINOM school. The investigation revealed the teenager had planned the attack in advance. The victim sustained five stab wounds to her back and neck.

item.title: Foreigners Used Stolen IDs to Register for Delivery Services in Almaty
item.description: Police in Almaty have apprehended a suspect accused of creating fake documents for delivery couriers and drivers. The 32-year-old allegedly used real Kazakhstani identification numbers but altered photos and personal details. This allowed clients, primarily from Central and South Asia, to register for delivery and ride-sharing services anonymously.

item.title: Man Arrested in Almaty for Producing Fake Documents for Foreigners
item.description: A 32-year-old man has been arrested in Almaty for creating fake documents for foreign citizens. The suspect allegedly altered documents using valid Kazakh IINs and ID numbers, changing photos and personal data. His clients were primarily from Central and South Asian countries.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Build Low-Carbon Industrial Park in Naryn Region
item.description: A new industrial park for energy-intensive, low-carbon production will be built in Kyrgyzstan's Naryn region. The cabinet of ministers approved the project, aiming to attract foreign investment and support regional development. Changes were also made to regulations for free economic zones to facilitate investment.

item.title: Uzbekistan Establishes Procedures for Tourism Facilities Around Reservoirs
item.description: Uzbekistan has set regulations for organizing tourism facilities around reservoirs. Land plots for tourism services will be allocated via electronic online auctions. The plan includes establishing rescue services and implementing online booking and QR code navigation systems in these areas.

item.title: Chinese Consortium to Build Gas Processing Plant at Kashagan Field
item.description: QazaqGaz has signed an EPCC contract with a Chinese consortium for the construction of a gas processing plant with an annual capacity of 2.5 billion cubic meters at the Kashagan field. The plant will increase raw gas processing and supply of commercial gas, LPG, and sulfur to the domestic market.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Webcam studio owner admits bribing judges for sentence reduction
item.description: An activist claims Daniel Azhiev, owner of webcam studios, admitted to bribing three judges in the Chuy Regional Court to reduce his five-year sentence for drug use. Azhiev, initially sentenced to nine years for operating studios, has had his sentence reduced multiple times.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President explains dismissal of 'Uchkun' publishing house director
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov stated that the director of the 'Uchkun' publishing house was dismissed due to a shortage of textbooks. He noted that books were being sold in markets instead of being provided free to students. The president promised all students will receive textbooks within two years and plans for tablets in five years.

item.title: Kyrgyz Mother Seeks President's Help in Custody Battle for Daughters
item.description: Rayana Azamatova has asked Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov to help enforce a Supreme Court ruling granting her custody of her daughters. Her ex-husband took the girls in 2019; she has since recovered one but is still separated from the other, aged 12. A criminal case is pending against the ex-husband.

item.title: Almaty City to Expropriate Land for Street Extension and Park Renovation
item.description: Almaty's city administration will forcibly acquire several land plots to extend Tole Bi Street and renovate Seyfullin Park. Additional plots are also being acquired for a new construction project on Zharokov Street. The expropriation process is expected to be completed by the end of 2027 and 2028, respectively.

item.title: Two Detained in Osh Region for Extortion and Threats
item.description: Two individuals were apprehended in Kyrgyzstan's Osh region for allegedly threatening a resident with online video publication and demanding money. The suspects, born in 2003 and 2007, were caught while receiving a portion of the demanded sum. A criminal case for extortion has been initiated.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Replace Paper Textbooks with Tablets in Five Years
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to transition to electronic textbooks within five to six years, according to President Sadyr Japarov. The initiative aims to alleviate the burden of heavy backpacks on students. While tablet procurement is costly, they are expected to have a longer lifespan than traditional books.

item.title: Kazakhstan Updates Rules for Citizens Emigrating Abroad for Permanent Residence
item.description: Kazakhstan has revised the procedures for citizens wishing to move abroad for permanent residence. The Ministry of Internal Affairs has introduced new requirements for document submission and application processes, including grounds for service refusal. These updated regulations apply to Kazakh citizens, foreigners residing permanently in Kazakhstan, and stateless individuals. Applications can be submitted online via the eGov portal.

item.title: US Stock Market Plunges Over $3 Trillion After Democrats' Gains, AI Bubble Fears Grow
item.description: The US stock market experienced a significant decline, with the Nasdaq Composite dropping 5.5% and market capitalization reducing by $2.5 trillion. The PHLX Semiconductor index fell 12.25%, the largest drop since the pandemic. The S&P 500 decreased by 4.4%, marking its worst day since April 2025. Total market value for companies in the S&P Composite 1500 fell by $3.2 trillion.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev Holds Meetings in Astana on Regional Security
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held a series of meetings and discussions in Astana. Discussions focused on international and regional security, the fight against terrorism and extremism within the Aqaba process framework, and new threats associated with the development of artificial intelligence.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Armenia Discuss Connecting Middle Corridor with Trump Route
item.description: Kazakhstan and Armenia explored linking the Middle Corridor transport route with the TRIPP (Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity). This potential new route through Armenia aims to provide more delivery options for carriers and attract additional cargo. The discussion occurred during a visit by Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Transport.

item.title: US Unveils Broader European Security Plan Ahead of Ukraine Peace Talks
item.description: The White House announced a European security framework for Ukraine, including security assurances, ahead of trilateral peace talks with Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi. The proposal, detailed by Jared Kushner, emphasizes respect for sovereignty, crisis communication, and military transparency, while NATO remains central to European defense.

item.title: Bishkek Faces School Capacity Shortage Amidst Internal and External Migration
item.description: Bishkek is experiencing a shortage of school places due to a significant influx of 12,500 students from regions and abroad. Internal migration and the return of Kyrgyz citizens from foreign countries are straining the capital's educational institutions. The Ministry of Education states that approximately 50 more schools are needed, as current construction rates cannot keep pace with the growing student population.

item.title: Kazakhstan Vice President Addresses Al-Farabi Heritage Symposium in Almaty
item.description: Vice President Yerlan Karin participated in an international symposium dedicated to the philosophical and scientific legacy of Al-Farabi. The event, held at Al-Farabi Kazakh National University, emphasized the importance of studying and popularizing the thinker's ideas for younger generations and modern science. President Tokayev highlighted Al-Farabi's enduring values aligning with national identity concepts.

item.title: Sirajuddin Haqqani Attends Graduation Ceremony for Over 400 Students in Ghazni
item.description: Afghanistan's Interior Affairs Ministry reported that Sirajuddin Haqqani attended a graduation ceremony for more than 400 students at the Noor-ul-Madaris Madrasa in Ghazni province. Graduates received certificates, and Haqqani emphasized the importance of education and religious scholarship.

item.title: Bolat Utemuratov Acquires OLX Kazakhstan for $81 Million
item.description: Bolat Utemuratov has purchased OLX Kazakhstan for $81 million through Beeline Kazakhstan. The deal gives the new owner full control of the popular classifieds platform. Utemuratov stated the investment aims to develop digital service infrastructure. OLX Kazakhstan currently has approximately 9 million active users monthly.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Sees Off Uzbek President Mirziyoyev at Astana Airport
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev bid farewell to Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev at the Astana airport. Mirziyoyev was in Kazakhstan for a working visit to attend the Aqaba Process summit. The summit brought together leaders from Kazakhstan, Jordan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan, and Kyrgyzstan to discuss counter-terrorism efforts.
